a2-unit-43.43.1 A game of GHOST:
Kate: We have ten minutes before the train comes. How about playing a game?
Tom: OK. I know a good one. It's called GHOST. Do you know how to play?
Kate: No, I don't.
Tom: I can teach you. It's very easy. It's a spelling game. We have to take turns saying a letter to make a word. The aim is to make the other player finish the word. So, in your turn, you shouldn't say any letter that can be the last letter of a word.
Kate: But how do I know what word we're spelling?
Tom: You don't! That's the game. Let's start. I'll explain as we go along. The first letter is C.
Kate: OK. I'm going to say K for the second letter.
Tom: C K? You can't say that. There's no word in English that starts with those two letters. It must be a real word that you're thinking of. But you're not supposed to tell me the word.
Kate: OK, OK. Let's go for A. So it's C A. Can I say that?
Tom: Yes, that's fine. Lots of words start with those letters. C A... T.
Kate: That's a word! Cat! You lose!
Tom: Wait. There's one more rule that I haven't told you yet. Three-letter words don't count. So it's your turn again.
Kate: Really? You should explain that rule at the beginning! All right. Hmm... C A T C.
Tom: Ooh, that's difficult. Are you sure that's a real word? You can't say it if you don't know the word.
Kate: Yes, I'm definitely thinking of a real word. Do you want a clue?
Tom: You're not allowed to give me a clue. Let me think... Oh, I see what you're doing. You want me to say H, to make catch. I guess there's no other way to finish the word. You beat me!
Kate: I can't believe I won the game. I've never played before!
Tom: Wait. You haven't won the game yet. You just won the first round. Because I lost, I get the letter G. If I lose again, I get H, then O, then S, and then T. The first player to lose five rounds and get G H O S T loses the whole game.
Kate: I see. Well, I hope you're not going to get angry when you lose.
Tom: You don't have to be so annoying! Who says I'm going to lose?
a2-unit-43.43.2 Repeat: rules:
Narrator: We have to take turns.
Narrator: She has to choose a word.
Narrator: You're not supposed to tell me.
Narrator: You're not allowed to give a clue.
Narrator: You don't have to wait.
Narrator: You can't use your phone.
a2-unit-43.43.3 Necessary or not necessary?:
Narrator: Number one. You have to say a letter.
Narrator: Number two. You don't have to start with A.
Narrator: Number three. You must use real words.
Narrator: Number four. You don't have to write anything.
Narrator: Number five. You have to wait for your turn.
Narrator: Number six. You don't have to answer quickly.
